name: capability-placement-sweep
note: Frozen replayable corpus for #54. Refs are real closed tickets (all shipped agent:done — known-good). frozen_body is the task text as of freeze; difficulty is a curator judgment from scope + labels.

tickets.title: init/start: auto-create the GitHub pipeline labels
tickets.why: Create the GitHub pipeline labels via REST on init/start — mechanical, one command.
tickets.frozen_body:
GitHub's API won't add a label to an issue unless the label already exists in the repo, so today a user must hand-create every pipeline label (`agent:code`, `agent:review`, …) before `agenthook start` can move issues. This is documented as a gotcha in `docs/github-setup.md`, but it's avoidable.

**Proposal:** on `init` (or first `start`), read the pipeline's `sourceLabel`/`successLabel`/`failureLabel`/`holdLabel` values and create any missing labels in the repo via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels` (ignore 422 "already_exists").

- Adapter: `src/trackers/github.js`
- Wizard: `src/commands/init.js`
- This is the GitHub analog of Asana's "fill in the section gids" step — removing it is real onboarding friction.

_Surfaced while building the GitHub tracker (#labels-as-sections)._

tickets.title: doctor: flag unfilled TODO_* pipeline bindings
tickets.why: doctor warns on unfilled TODO_* bindings — single validation check.
tickets.frozen_body:
`agenthook doctor` checks the token, repo, port, and ingress — but not the pipeline bindings. So a freshly `init`-ed config (with `TODO_SOURCE_SECTION_GID` etc. still in place) **passes doctor yet silently does nothing**, because the placeholders never match an incoming event.

**Proposal:** add a doctor check that scans `cfg.pipeline[]` and fails (or loudly warns) when any binding (`source*`/`success*`/`failure*`/`hold*`) is empty or still a `TODO_*` placeholder. Cheap, and it closes the most common first-run trap.

- File: `src/commands/doctor.js`

tickets.title: ah agents: tighten process match — substring "claude -p" yields false positives
tickets.why: Tighten `ah agents` process match — substring "claude -p" false positives.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`src/commands/agents.js:15` filters with `cmd.includes("claude -p")` — a loose **substring**
match. Any process whose argv merely *contains* that string is counted, e.g. a shell running a
command that mentions it.

**Observed:** a transient pid was counted as an agent with `step=?  ref=?` (neither field
resolved) — it was an unrelated shell whose command text happened to contain `claude -p`, not a
spawned agent.

## Expected

Match only the real spawned agents the receiver launches (`src/dispatch.js`), not arbitrary
command lines that mention the string.

## Suggested approach

- Anchor on the **binary invocation**, not a substring: e.g. `/(^|\/)claude\s+-p\b/` so the
  claude bin must start the command, not appear mid-line.
- Or require a co-marker the dispatched prompt always carries (`Ref:` / `=== TICKET ===` /
  `--dangerously-skip-permissions`) **and** the claude bin.
- A row that resolves neither `step` nor `ref` (both `?`) is a strong false-positive signal —
  at minimum drop those from the count.

## Acceptance

- A shell whose command text contains `claude -p` is **not** counted.
- Real spawned agents still listed with their `step` + `ref`.
- Offline unit test: feed crafted `ps` lines (one real agent, one decoy shell) → only the real
  one is counted.

_Found by dogfooding agenthook on itself while reviewing PR #5. Note: same file as the
profile-scoping issue — sequence the two fixes to avoid a merge conflict._

tickets.title: catchup falsely reports "dispatched" when the item is in no source stage (silent no-op)
tickets.why: catchup falsely reports "dispatched" for items in no source stage — localized fix.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`agenthook catchup <ref>` forges an `issues/opened` (GitHub) event, POSTs it to the server, and
prints `dispatched <ref>` on the 200 fast-ACK. But the server routes the forged event **by the
item's current labels / section / status** — if the item is not in any step's source stage, no step
matches and the event is **silently dropped**. The CLI still reports success.

### Verified

`catchup 7` on an assigned-but-unlabeled issue (no `agent:code`):

```
POST /github/ -> 200
dispatched 7. The server routes it to the step its current section maps to.
```

…but nothing spawned — queue stayed `0 running, 0 queued`, no worktree, #7 unchanged. The
"dispatched" reflects the HTTP ACK, not the routing outcome.

## Proposal

- Before POSTing, `catchup` pre-checks the item's current stage against the pipeline's source
  stages; if none match, report:
  `#<ref> is not in any pipeline source stage — nothing to replay. Use 'agenthook run <ref> [step]' to start it.`
  (links #11) and exit non-zero.
- **Or** the engine returns the routing result (matched `stepId`, or `dropped`) in the ACK body and
  `catchup` prints that instead of a blind "dispatched".

## Acceptance

- `catchup` on an item **not** in a source stage prints the explicit "nothing to replay / use run"
  message and is clearly distinguished from a real dispatch (non-zero exit).
- `catchup` on an item that **is** in a source stage still works and reports the matched step.

_Found while dogfooding. Pairs with #11 (the `run` verb) and the docs clarification._

tickets.title: `<command> --help` runs the command instead of showing help (start --help boots the server)
tickets.why: Arg-parse bug: `<command> --help` runs the command instead of showing help.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`agenthook <command> --help` (and `-h`) **runs the command** instead of printing usage. Help is only intercepted when it is the *first* token; a `--help` sitting after a subcommand is ignored and the command body executes. For `start` this means `agenthook start --help` **boots the receiver** (ingress tunnel + webhook register + serve) — a real side effect when the user only wanted help. Every subcommand is affected (`doctor --help` runs the preflight, etc.).

## Evidence

- `bin/agenthook.js:93` — help is intercepted only as the first token: `if (!cmd || cmd === "help" || cmd === "--help" || cmd === "-h")`.
- `bin/agenthook.js:97,102` — `cmd` resolves to `fn` and `await fn(parse(rest))` runs unconditionally; a `--help` in `rest` is never checked.
- `src/commands/` — grep of `.help` is empty: **no command reads `args.help`**, so the flag is silently dropped and the body runs.
- `src/commands/start.js:29` -> `await createEngine(cfg).serve()` — confirms `start --help` boots the server.
- Detail for the fix: `parse()` (`bin/agenthook.js:50`) only treats `--`-prefixed tokens as flags, so `-h` becomes a **positional** in `args._`, not `{help:true}`. The guard must inspect the **raw `rest` array** (pre-parse), where both `--help` and `-h` appear verbatim — not rely on `parse()`.

## Proposed change

A pure dispatch-layer guard in `bin/agenthook.js`, no command behavior touched:

- Add a small exported pure helper `wantsHelp(rest)` -> boolean: `rest.includes("--help") || rest.includes("-h")`. Export it (and/or `parse`) so the dispatch layer is unit-testable without spawning a server — currently `parse`/`main`/`COMMANDS`/`HELP` are not exported and the file runs `main()` on import.
- In `main()`, after `cmd` resolves to `fn` and **before** `await fn(...)`: `if (wantsHelp(rest)) { console.log(HELP); return; }`.
- Printing the global `HELP` is the acceptable minimum; a per-command usage line keyed off `cmd` is a nice-to-have, not required.
- Match existing ESM + JSDoc/`checkJs` conventions; keep `npm run typecheck` green.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `agenthook start --help` prints usage and does **not** boot the receiver (no ingress/webhook/serve side effect).
- [ ] `agenthook <command> --help` and `<command> -h` print usage and do not execute the command, for every subcommand.
- [ ] `agenthook --help` / `-h` / `help` / no-arg still print usage (unchanged).
- [ ] `--version` / `-v` still print the version (unchanged).
- [ ] Real flags still work: `start --detach`, `agents --all`, `cleanup --apply`, `catchup <ref> --force`, `--config <path>`.
- [ ] A unit test on the arg/dispatch layer asserts `wantsHelp(["--help"])` / `wantsHelp(["-h"])` are true and a real-flag-only `rest` (e.g. `["--detach"]`) is false — i.e. `<cmd> --help` resolves to help, not command execution.

_Found by hand while looking for the background flag (`--detach`)._

tickets.title: ah agents: live token tally floors sub-1000 to 0k — needle stuck
tickets.why: One-line display bug: live token tally floors sub-1000 to 0k.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`ah agents` shows a live per-agent token tally (from running.json, updated per stream event). But `fmtTok` k-rounds everything: `Math.round(n / 1000)k`. A running agent with input=2, output=377 renders `tok=0k/0k` — reads as "no data" when it's really "<1k so far". Since users watch this live (`watch -n 10 ah agents`), the needle sits at 0k for the whole early phase of a run, then jumps. The live tally is the feature; the formatter hides it.

## Evidence

- `src/commands/agents.js` — `export function fmtTok(input, output, costUsd)`: `const k = (n = 0) => \`${Math.round(n / 1000)}k\`;` — floors any n<500 to `0k`, any n<1500 to `1k`.
- Observed live: running.json `{input:2, output:377}` → `ah agents` prints `tok=0k/0k`.

## Proposed change

Make the small-scale end legible so the needle moves from the first tokens. In `fmtTok` (agents.js), for values under 1000 show a finer scale rather than flooring to `0k`. Options (pick one, keep it compact):
- **Decimals under 1k**: `377 → 0.4k`, `2 → 0.0k` (or raw `2`).
- **Raw hundreds under 1k**: `377 → 377`, switch to `k` at ≥1000.

Prefer whichever keeps column width stable and the needle visibly moving on a 10s watch. Keep the `≥1000 → Nk` behavior and the `-`/dash for genuinely-absent data (null input AND output). Cost formatting unchanged.

Scope: the live per-agent formatter only. `ls.js`/`status.js` `fmtTokens` (M/K) format large *totals* — out of scope unless the same flooring bites there.

## Acceptance

- A running agent with a few hundred output tokens shows a non-zero, moving value on successive `ah agents` calls (not `0k/0k`).
- `≥1000` still renders as `Nk`; genuinely-absent data still renders `-`.
- `fmtTok` unit tests updated to cover the sub-1000 range (existing tests live in `test/agents.test.js`).

tickets.title: docs: getting-started effort guidance is backwards (says high for code)
tickets.why: Docs correction: getting-started effort guidance was backwards.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`docs/getting-started.md:129-131` advises the **opposite** of the effort placement the project researched, shipped, and now has data supporting. Current text:

> `effort` … Spend tokens where they matter: `"low"`/`"medium"` for `triage`/`review`, `"high"` for `code`.

This tells users to run **cheap triage, expensive code** — the back-loaded strategy. The dogfood config and the effort-placement research concluded the reverse (front-load): **`triage` high, `review` medium, `code` low with a difficulty-gated escalation to high only for hard tickets**. Following the doc as written wastes tokens on implementation (already pinned by a good spec) and starves the spec/design stage where errors compound.

## Evidence

- `docs/getting-started.md:131` — `"high"` for `code`.
- Shipped dogfood tiering (front-loaded): `triage` opus/high, `code` sonnet/low + `escalate.hard → opus/high`, `review` opus/medium (see `agenthook.config.example.json` / the pipeline `//` comments added with #53/#55).
- Dogfood token data backs it: triage ~\$0.62–0.80/run vs code (sonnet) ~\$0.45–0.68/run — the expensive stage is deliberately the front (`ah usage`).

## Proposed change

Rewrite the guidance in `getting-started.md` to describe front-loading:
- `triage` — high (the spec is the leverage point; a bad spec no downstream stage recovers).
- `code` — low/base, because a precise triage spec makes implementation mechanical; escalate to high **only** for `hard` tickets via the `escalate` map (point at #53/#55).
- `review` — medium, anchored on running tests (the oracle catches what the model doesn't).

Keep it short. Link to `usage.md` for the cost data that motivates it. Do not change any config defaults — this is a docs-only correction.

## Acceptance

- `getting-started.md` no longer recommends `"high"` for `code`.
- New text names the front-load rationale and the `escalate`-for-hard exception.
- No code/config changes.

tickets.title: ah agents: scope to the active profile (or label each line with its owner)
tickets.why: Scope `ah agents` to the active profile (or label each line) — process listing + config.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`agents()` (`src/commands/agents.js`) takes no `cfg` and greps `ps` **system-wide** for
`claude -p`, printing every match in one undifferentiated list (line 18 has no profile/owner
column). So `ah agents` run under one profile reports **other profiles'** agents.

**Observed:** the `agenthook-dogfood` profile showed `── 2 agent(s) running ──` while its own
queue was `0 running, 0 queued`. The processes belonged to a co-running `alephbeta` (Asana)
profile — `cwd = /home/.../workspace/alephbeta-agents/<gid>`, ref = an Asana task gid, not a
GitHub issue number. Misleading: looks like the dogfood is busy when it is idle.

## Expected

`ah agents` reports the **active profile's** agents by default; or at minimum tags each line
with the owning profile.

## Suggested approach

- Accept `cfg` and cross-reference the profile's `running.json` (in-flight refs per profile) to
  filter/attribute — cross-platform, no `/proc` dependency (the file header touts cross-platform
  `ps`, so avoid Linux-only `/proc/<pid>/cwd`).
- Keep a `--all` flag for the current global view, each line labelled with its profile.

## Acceptance

- `ah agents` lists only the active profile's agents (refs present in this profile's `running.json`).
- `--all` keeps the cross-profile list, each row labelled with its profile name.
- Offline unit test: stub `ps` stdout + a `running.json` fixture; assert filtering + `--all`.

_Found by dogfooding agenthook on itself while reviewing PR #5._

tickets.title: Add `agenthook run <ref> [stepId]`: inject work into a step (assign + enter source stage)
tickets.why: New `agenthook run <ref> [stepId]` subcommand — inject work into a step.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

There is no first-class way to **start** pipeline work on a backlog item. To kick off a NEW item you
must manually (a) assign it to the token's own account (fail-closed scoping) **and** (b) move it into
the first step's **source stage** — add the source label (GitHub), move to the source section
(Asana), or transition to the source status (Jira) — via the tracker UI or `gh`/API.

`catchup`/`reconcile` look like they would do this but do not: they only replay items **already**
resting in a source stage. (Verified while dogfooding: `reconcile` → `board clean — no resting
tasks`; `catchup <ref>` on an unlabeled issue falsely printed `dispatched` and spawned nothing.)

## Proposal

Add `agenthook run <ref> [stepId]` (alias `kick` / `start-step`):

- Resolve the target step — default the pipeline's **first** step, or the one named by `stepId`.
- Ensure the item is assigned to us (assign if needed; `--no-assign` to skip), satisfying fail-closed
  scoping.
- Move the item **into** that step's source stage via the adapter — reuse the same stage-set
  primitive `advance` already uses (GitHub: add source label; Asana: `addTask` to source section;
  Jira: transition to source status).
- The live webhook then fires the step normally — no special dispatch path.

**Blind-engine fit:** add one adapter method (e.g. `enterStage(ref, stageGid)`), or reuse the
label/section/status setter `advance` already has, so the engine stays tracker-agnostic.

## Acceptance

- `agenthook run 42` assigns #42 to us (if needed) + puts it in the first step's source stage → the
  receiver spawns that step.
- `agenthook run 42 review` targets the `review` step's source stage.
- Works for all three trackers (label / section / status).
- Clear error if the ref doesn't exist; if no server is up, says the item now rests in the stage and
  will be picked up on `reconcile`.

_Found while dogfooding (the maxConcurrent=2 exercise): labeling was the only way to start backlog
items. Pairs with the catchup-reporting fix and the docs clarification._

tickets.title: `ah run` has no guard against re-injecting an item already in the pipeline (double-dispatch races: shared ref-keyed worktree + clobbered running.json)
tickets.why: Idempotency guard: `ah run` must not re-inject an item already in the pipeline.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

`agenthook run <ref>` blindly assigns + enters the step's source stage **even if the item is
already in the pipeline** (carries a pipeline label and/or has a running job). Running it twice — or
running an item that's already mid-flow — **double-dispatches**: two agents race on the same ref,
and because the worktree and crash-recovery state are keyed by `ref`, they collide.

### Observed (real incident, monitoring #19)

`ah run 19` was invoked twice (the first run had already advanced triage→code). The second run
re-added `agent:triage` on top of the in-flight `agent:code`:

- **Two agents ran on ref 19 at once** (`step=code` + `step=triage`).
- Both used `agenthook-worktrees/19` — the worktree is **keyed by ref**, so the two code agents
  shared ONE worktree and clobbered each other's commits.
- `running.json` is **keyed by ref** (`{"19": {...}}`), so the second job's `setRunning` overwrote
  the first's crash-recovery entry.
- Labels thrashed (`agent:code` + `agent:triage` both present), cascaded through the pipeline, and
  produced a clobbered draft PR.

### Root cause

- `src/commands/run.js` calls `enterStage` unconditionally — no check that the ref is already in a
  source stage or already running.
- `src/worktree.js` keys the worktree by `ref` (intended so steps in ONE flow reuse it — but two
  concurrent jobs on a ref then collide).
- `src/store.js` keys `running.json` in-flight jobs by `ref` (one entry per ref).

## Proposed change

1. **Guard `run`:** before `enterStage`, fetch the item and **refuse (or require `--force`)** if it
   already carries ANY pipeline label, or if `running.json` has an entry for the ref:
   `#<ref> is already in the pipeline (agent:code / running) — finish or reset it first, or pass --force.`
2. Defense-in-depth: the engine could drop a trigger for a ref that already has a running job for a
   *different* step (dedup by ref, not only by dedupKey).
3. Document the invariant: **one ref = one in-flight flow** (worktree + running.json are per-ref by
   design).

## Acceptance

- `ah run <ref>` on an item already carrying a pipeline label (or already running) refuses with a
  clear message and does NOT re-dispatch — unless `--force`.
- The happy path (a clean backlog item) still dispatches.
- A unit test covers the guard (mock `fetchTask` returning a pipeline label / `running.json` having
  the ref → run refuses).

_Found while monitoring #19 through the new 3-step pipeline — a double `ah run 19` raced and cascaded._

tickets.title: github tracker: respect issue blocking (blocked_by gate + close-release)
tickets.why: GitHub tracker respects issue blocking (blocked_by gate + close-release).
tickets.frozen_body:
## Goal

Make the **`github` (labels) tracker respect issue blocking relationships**: an issue that is
`blocked_by` an open issue must NOT fire its pipeline step until every blocker is resolved, and the
moment the last blocker closes its dependents fire automatically. No polling, no `reconcile` step.

Live test case already on the board: **#37, #38, #39, #40 are `blocked_by #36`** (native GitHub
issue dependencies, already set). With this change, starting the server must run #36 alone; #37-#40
only fire after #36 closes.

## Mechanism (all in `src/trackers/github.js` — engine/dispatch stay blind, no interface change)

GitHub native issue dependencies are live on this repo:
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by` → issues that block `n`
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocking` → issues that `n` blocks

The one repo webhook already subscribes to the whole `issues` event, so the `closed` action is
**already delivered** — `processEvents` just filters it out today. No webhook reconfig.

### 1. Block gate
Add a helper `blockedBy(ref)` → GET `…/dependencies/blocked_by`, keep entries whose `state === "open"`,
return their numbers. In `processEvents`, on the `opened`/`reopened`/`assigned` and `labeled` paths,
**after** resolving the step and the assignee check: if `await blockedBy(ref)` is non-empty, log
`[blocked] #<ref> blocked by #<n>… — resting` and **emit no job** (`return []`). The issue stays in
its source label; no agent spawns. Checked live per event, so reopen/multi-blocker stay correct.

### 2. Close-release
Handle `ev.action === "closed"`: GET `…/dependencies/blocking` for the closed issue → its dependents.
For each dependent that (a) is ours (`issueIsOurs`), (b) now has empty `blockedBy`, and (c) currently
rests in a step's source label (`stepForLabels` over its live labels), emit a re-fire job:
`{ kind: "pipeline", ref: dep, stepId: step.id, dedupKey: `unblock:${ref}:${dep}` }`.
So closing #36 fires #37-#40.

### 3. Terminal step closes the issue (so an agent-finished blocker auto-releases)
The `done` step is `manual` + terminal. Make reaching it CLOSE the GitHub issue (PATCH issue
`state:"closed"`), so a blocker that finishes its pipeline triggers the close-release above without a
human. Cleanest: in `advance`, after the label move, if the entered step (the one whose `sourceLabel`
== the new label) is the terminal/manual step, `PATCH /issues/{ref}` `{state:"closed"}`. Gate behind a
per-step flag (e.g. `closeIssue: true` on the `done` step in config) so it's explicit, not implicit.

### 4. Gate the reconcile path too
`listResting` returns jobs straight to `intake` (bypasses `processEvents`), so it must skip any ref
with a non-empty `blockedBy` — otherwise `reconcile` re-injects blocked issues.

## Acceptance

- With #37-#40 `blocked_by #36` and all five labeled `agent:triage`, starting the server runs **only
  #36**; #37-#40 stay resting (logged `[blocked]`).
- Closing #36 (manually OR via the `done` step) fires #37-#40.
- An issue with two blockers stays blocked until BOTH close.
- Reopening a blocker re-blocks dependents on their next event.
- `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` green; `node --check` clean.

## Tests

Unit-test `blockedBy` filtering (open vs closed) and the close-release fan-out target selection with a
stubbed `api`/`json` (mirror the existing tracker test style — pure, no network). Keep parsing of the
dependency payloads behind the adapter's local `json(res)=>any` helper.

## Notes
- `github` tracker only for now (Asana/Jira/Projects v2 unchanged).
- No new engine or `types.js` interface methods — the gate lives entirely inside `github.js`.
- Ground in `src/trackers/github.js` (`processEvents`, `advance`, `listResting`) + the asana.js
  reference doc-comment for the adapter contract.

tickets.title: dispatch: per-step effort level (claude -p --effort) to optimize token usage
tickets.why: Per-step effort level plumbed through dispatch (claude -p --effort).
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

A pipeline runs every step at Claude's default reasoning effort. There's no way to spend
tokens where they matter — e.g. cheap `low`/`medium` for `triage`/`review`, `high` for `code`.
Add a per-step **`effort`** field that passes through to `claude -p --effort <level>`, exactly
mirroring the existing per-step `model` passthrough. Engine and adapters stay provider-blind;
the change is contained to `src/dispatch.js` + `src/types.js` (+ docs/tests).

## Evidence (read against the tree)

- `src/dispatch.js:44-67` — `spawnClaude({ prompt, cwd, logPath, model, verdictFile, onPid })`
  builds `args` and pushes `--model` at **`src/dispatch.js:47`**: `if (model) args.push("--model", model);`.
  The new flag mirrors this line.
- `src/dispatch.js:162-170` — `runClaude` calls `spawnClaude({ …, model: step.model, … })` at
  **`src/dispatch.js:166`**. `effort: step.effort` goes beside it.
- `src/types.js:23-45` — the step typedef is named **`Step`** (the issue called it `StepDef`;
  no such typedef exists). The per-step `model` lives at **`src/types.js:30`**
  (`@property {string} [model]`); add `effort` right after.
- CLI check: `claude --effort <level>` exists in 2.1.196 with levels
  **`low, medium, high, xhigh, max`** (verified via `claude --help`). Invalid value → CLI warns + default.
- `agenthook.config.example.json:60` — the `review` step already carries `"model": "claude-opus-4-8"`,
  so an `"effort"` sibling has a natural home.

### Testability gap (resolve in this ticket)

`spawnClaude` is a **closure inside `createDispatcher`** — `src/dispatch.js:36` is the only
export. There is **no existing dispatch/spawn test** to mirror (`test/run.test.js` tests
`entryBlock` from `commands/run.js`, not dispatch), and argv is built inline, so it can't be
asserted without spawning real `claude`. The fix: extract a small **pure exported helper**, e.g.
`export function buildClaudeArgs({ model, effort, fullAuto })` returning the `args` array, and
have `spawnClaude` call it. This is additive (no behavior change) and makes the argv unit-testable
with no real spawn.

## Proposed change (minimal, additive)

1. **`src/types.js`** — add to the `Step` typedef, after the `model` line:
   `@property {'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'|'max'} [effort]  per-step `claude -p --effort` override`
2. **`src/dispatch.js`**
   - Extract `buildClaudeArgs({ model, effort, fullAuto })` (exported, pure) that builds the
     `["-p", prompt]`-style flag list. Validate `effort` against the union
     `['low','medium','high','xhigh','max']` before pushing — invalid → `console.warn` + omit the
     flag (fall back to CLI default; never crash). Push `--effort` **after** `--model`,
     `--dangerously-skip-permissions` after, preserving current order.
   - `spawnClaude` gains an `effort` param and uses the helper to build `args`.
   - `runClaude` (`src/dispatch.js:166`) passes `effort: step.effort` into `spawnClaude`.
3. **Docs** — document `effort` on a step in the config docs (e.g. `docs/getting-started.md` or
   the provider setup docs), with a worked example (`triage`/`review`: `low`/`medium`, `code`:
   `high`). Optional: add `"effort"` to a step in `agenthook.config.example.json`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A step with `"effort": "low"` spawns `claude -p … --effort low`; a step with **no** `effort`
      spawns with **no** `--effort` flag (current default behavior unchanged).
- [ ] An invalid `effort` value (e.g. `"turbo"`) is dropped with a `console.warn` and **no**
      `--effort` flag passed — dispatch never crashes.
- [ ] `--effort` is pushed after `--model` and before/after the existing flags consistently;
      `--model`-only and no-flag cases are unaffected.
- [ ] `claudeBin` remains overridable (unchanged).
- [ ] Unit test in `test/` asserts the built argv (no real `claude` spawn): `--effort` present when
      set, absent when unset, omitted+warned when invalid — via the exported `buildClaudeArgs`.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` green; `node --check bin/agenthook.js src/**/*.js` clean.

## Notes

Tracker-agnostic: `dispatch.js` is provider-blind, so this works for asana/jira/github/
github-projects alike — no engine or adapter change.

tickets.title: flow: done-step closeIssue closes the issue before its PR merges (issue-state ≠ merge-state)
tickets.why: Ordering bug: done-step closeIssue closes before its PR merges.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Observed

With `done` flagged `closeIssue: true`, reaching `agent:done` CLOSES the GitHub issue. But the PR is
**not** merged at that point — it waits for a human. Result this round: #37, #38, #39, #46 are **closed**
while PRs #43/#44/#45/#48 are still **open/unmerged**. Issue state says "done"; the work isn't integrated.

For sub-issue parents (#36) this also ticks the checklist as complete on unmerged work.

## Question / options

Is "done" meant to be *agent-work-complete (PR ready)* or *merged*? Pick the model:

1. **Keep close-on-done** but treat issue-close as "agent finished, PR ready for human" — document it so a
   closed issue + open PR is expected, not a bug. (closeIssue stays for dependent-release.)
2. **Close only on merge** — done step parks at `agent:done` (don't close); a merge (or a `gh pr merge`
   hook) closes the issue. Keeps issue-state == integration-state.
3. **Auto-merge on done** (optional per-step `mergeOnDone`) — agent review passed → merge the PR → issue
   closes naturally. Most "moving", most risk under fullAuto.

Note: `closeIssue` was added for the blocked-dependent **release** path (epic #36 now uses sub-issues,
not blocking, so that path is dormant here — the premature close is the only visible effect right now).

## Notes
- Backlog/design decision — unarmed. Affects `src/dispatch.js` (manual/done branch) + the github `advance`
  close + the `closeIssue` semantics in docs.

tickets.title: tokens: ah usage command with daily/weekly summaries
tickets.why: New `ah usage` command with daily/weekly aggregation.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Problem

Per-run token/cost records land in `usage.jsonl` (written by `store.recordUsage`, one JSON
line per finished run — see `src/store.js:125` and `buildUsageRecord` at `src/dispatch.js:147`),
but nothing surfaces them. Users have no way to see what runs cost. Add an `ah usage` subcommand
that reads those records and prints per-run rows plus day/week rollups — pure local aggregation,
no network.

## Evidence

- `src/store.js:128` — `readUsage()` already exists: returns the parsed array (tolerates a
  partial trailing line), `[]` when the file is absent. The command consumes this; no store change needed.
- `src/dispatch.js:147` — `buildUsageRecord` fixes the record shape each line has:
  `{ ref, stepId, model, startedAt, endedAt, durationMs, input, output, cacheRead, cacheCreate, costUsd, sessionId }`.
  `costUsd`, `model`, `durationMs`, `sessionId` may be `undefined`; `input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreate`
  default to `0`. Aggregation must tolerate missing `costUsd`/`model`.
- `bin/agenthook.js:73` — `COMMANDS` map; register the new command there.
- `bin/agenthook.js:43` — `VALUE_FLAGS = new Set(["config", "limit"])`. `--ref` takes a value,
  so **add `"ref"` to `VALUE_FLAGS`** or `--ref 58` swallows nothing. `--day`/`--week` are boolean flags (already handled).
- `bin/agenthook.js:77` — `HELP` string; add a `usage` line.
- `src/commands/status.js:10` — command signature convention: `export async function <name>(args)`,
  positional args via `args._[0]`, config via `loadConfig({ configPath: args.config })`. `cfg.dataDir`
  is where `usage.jsonl` lives; get the store via the same `makeStore(cfg.dataDir)` path other commands use.

## Proposed change

- New `src/commands/usage.js` — `export async function usage(args)`. Load config, read records via
  `store.readUsage()`. Keep display in the command; put pure aggregation in small **exported**
  helpers (so they unit-test without I/O).
  - **default**: table of recent runs — columns ref, step, model, in / out / cacheRead / cacheCreate
    tokens, $ (costUsd, `—` when undefined). Newest last (or respect `--limit`, already a value flag).
  - `--ref <n>`: filter records to one task (every step's spend), same table + totals row.
  - `--day`: group by calendar day (UTC date from `startedAt`); `--week`: group by ISO week.
    Each group row = summed tokens + $, with a per-model split. `--day` and `--week` are mutually
    exclusive (if both given, pick one deterministically or error — decide in code, keep it simple).
  - Always print a **totals** row (sum of tokens + $).
  - Empty/absent `usage.jsonl` → friendly `no usage recorded yet` and clean exit.
- Register `usage` in `bin/agenthook.js` `COMMANDS`, add `"ref"` to `VALUE_FLAGS`, add a `HELP` line.

Match repo conventions: ESM only, JSDoc types kept green under `npm run typecheck`, no new deps.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `ah usage` prints recent runs with token columns + $; totals row present.
- [ ] `ah usage --ref <n>` filters to one task's runs.
- [ ] `ah usage --day` and `--week` print correctly grouped totals (tokens + $) with a per-model split.
- [ ] Empty/absent `usage.jsonl` prints a friendly "no usage recorded yet", exits 0.
- [ ] `--ref` added to `VALUE_FLAGS` so it captures its value.
- [ ] Aggregation helpers unit-tested (`test/usage.test.js`) over a fixture record set covering
      missing `costUsd`/`model` and multi-day/-week/-model spread.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` green.

## Notes

`blocked_by` #61 (usage capture) — **now merged**, so unblocked. Difficulty: medium.

tickets.title: github-projects: core adapter — GraphQL client + authenticate + fetchTask + processEvents(Status routing) + advance(set Status)
tickets.why: github-projects core adapter: GraphQL client + authenticate + fetchTask.
tickets.frozen_body:
Part of #23 (GitHub Projects v2 tracker). **Foundation — the rest of the epic depends on this.**

## Scope

Scaffold `src/trackers/github-projects.js` and register `github-projects` in
`src/trackers/index.js` `TRACKERS`. Implement the live **event → move** core:

- **GraphQL client** — `POST https://api.github.com/graphql`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`,
  a local `gql(query, vars)` helper (mirror each adapter's `json(res)` pattern; responses are
  `any`). Resolve the project by `owner/number` (org or user) to its node id once, memoised.
- **`describe()`** — platform words for the blind prompt builders (issue/board/status).
- **`authenticate(ctx)`** — `x-hub-signature-256` constant-time verify (reuse the `github`
  pattern); handshake/secret handling as needed. Sync, no network.
- **`fetchTask(ref)`** — GraphQL the item/issue: `{ name, description, url, completed,
  assignedToUs, ref }`. `ref` is the underlying **issue number** (agents work the issue).
- **`processEvents(ctx)`** — parse a `projects_v2_item` event (`created`/`edited`), read the
  item's **Status** single-select value via GraphQL, and route to the step whose `sourceStatus`
  matches (case-insensitive). Dedup keys: `step:<id>:<ref>` (entered) / `secmove:<delivery>`
  (status changed). Ignore non-Status field edits and items whose content isn't an issue.
- **`advance(ref, stepId, verdict)`** — `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` mutation setting the
  Status single-select to the option for the outcome (`advance`→successStatus, `fail`→failure,
  `hold`→hold, `changes`→target step's sourceStatus). **Single-occupancy** — just set the option,
  no add-before-remove. An unknown/unset option name is a logged no-op (like Jira's unreachable
  transition).
- **Fail-closed scoping** — `isOurs`/`issueIsOurs` on the underlying issue's assignee, exactly like
  `github`; gate every mutation; unresolved identity → refuse.

Steps bind the existing `sourceStatus`/`successStatus`/`failureStatus`/`holdStatus` Step fields
(reused from Jira). ProviderConfig gains `project` (owner/number or URL) — add to `src/types.js`.

## Acceptance

- `tracker.type: "github-projects"` loads; a `projects_v2_item` Status-change event for an item in
  a step's source Status produces a `{kind:'pipeline', ref, stepId, dedupKey}` job.
- A non-Status edit, or an item not assigned to us, produces **no** job.
- `advance` issues the `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` mutation to the correct option per outcome.
- `npm run typecheck` green; offline unit covers route + advance (stub `global.fetch`/GraphQL).

tickets.title: github-projects: webhook lifecycle — org/user projects_v2_item hook + signing secret (manual fallback)
tickets.why: github-projects webhook lifecycle: org/user projects_v2_item hook + signing.
tickets.frozen_body:
Part of #23. **Depends on the core adapter (#30, landed).**

## Problem

The `github-projects` adapter exists but cannot stand up its own webhook: `registerWebhook` only
**prints** manual setup and `unregisterWebhooks` is a no-op — the header even calls auto-registration
"a later epic step." This issue is that step: auto-create (or find) the **`projects_v2_item`** webhook
for an **org-owned** project, signed with the already-generated secret, and scrub only our own stale
hooks on the boot re-register. Where the token lacks `admin:org_hook`, fall back gracefully to printed
manual instructions instead of crashing the receiver.

## Evidence (read)

- `src/trackers/github-projects.js:426-447` — `registerWebhook` is a manual-print stub today.
- `src/trackers/github-projects.js:449-452` — `unregisterWebhooks` is a no-op.
- `src/trackers/github-projects.js:26-28` — header comment: auto-registration deferred to "a later epic step."
- `src/trackers/github-projects.js:84-97` — `webhookSecret()` **already** generates + stores the secret
  under `github-projects:webhookSecret`; `verify()` (`:72-82`) + `authenticate()` (`:287-295`) **already**
  check `x-hub-signature-256`. So secret + verification are DONE — this issue only needs to pass the
  secret into the created hook's `config.secret`.
- `src/trackers/github-projects.js:43-51` — only a GraphQL `gql` helper exists; REST calls need a sibling.
- `src/trackers/github-projects.js:113-120` — the project probe queries `organization` AND `user` but
  discards which root resolved; it must record `ownerType` so `registerWebhook` picks the endpoint.
- Reference pattern: `src/trackers/github.js:210-222` (`deleteOurHooks`) + `:393-412` (scrub-then-create);
  graceful-manual tone: `src/trackers/jira.js:338-358`.

## Correction to the original scope (user projects)

The original ask said "user project → the user-level hook equivalent." There is **no such endpoint**:
GitHub's REST API exposes only **repo** (`/repos/.../hooks`) and **org** (`/orgs/{org}/hooks`) webhooks,
and `projects_v2_item` is **not** a repo-webhook event — it is delivered only by an **org webhook** or a
**GitHub App**. Personal accounts have no webhook settings UI either. So **user-owned** Projects v2 cannot
be auto- or manually-registered with a PAT at all; that path is GitHub-App territory and out of scope here.
Scope this issue to **org-owned** projects + a clear, non-crashing message for the user-owned case.

## Proposed change

In `src/trackers/github-projects.js`:

1. Add a REST helper beside `gql` — `rest(path, opts)` → `https://api.github.com{path}` with
   `Authorization: Bearer <token>` + `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`.
2. Extend the project-id probe (`:113-120`) to memoise `ownerType` (`"org"` | `"user"`) from whichever
   root (`organization` / `user`) resolved the id.
3. Add `deleteOurHooks()` mirroring `github.js:210` but against `/orgs/{org}/hooks?per_page=100`, deleting
   only hooks whose `config.url` (trailing slash stripped) ends with `/github-projects`.
4. `registerWebhook(url)`:
   - **org owner**: `deleteOurHooks()` then `POST /orgs/{org}/hooks` with
     `{ name:"web", active:true, events:["projects_v2_item"], config:{ url:"<ingress>/github-projects",
     content_type:"json", insecure_ssl:"0", secret? } }`. On **403/404** (missing `admin:org_hook`),
     **catch and print** the existing manual instructions — do **not** throw (the receiver must keep serving).
   - **user owner**: print a clear message that PAT/UI webhooks aren't available for user-owned Projects v2
     (org ownership or a GitHub App required); no crash.
5. `unregisterWebhooks()`: for an org owner with scope, `deleteOurHooks()`; otherwise no-op (mirror `github.js:414`).
6. Update the header comment (`:26-28`) — auto-registration is now done for the org case.

Match repo conventions (ESM, JSDoc types, `gql`/`rest` returning `any`). Keep `npm run typecheck` green.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Org project + token with `admin:org_hook`: `agenthook start` scrubs our stale `/github-projects`
      org hooks, then creates **one** `projects_v2_item` org hook at the ingress URL, signed with the
      stored secret. Re-running does not duplicate it.
- [ ] Missing `admin:org_hook` (403/404): prints copy-pasteable manual org-webhook instructions (payload
      URL, content-type `application/json`, secret, the "Projects v2 item" event); receiver keeps running.
- [ ] User-owned project: prints a clear "not supported with a PAT (use org ownership or a GitHub App)"
      message; no crash.
- [ ] Boot scrub deletes only hooks whose target URL ends `/github-projects`; unrelated org hooks untouched.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` + existing adapter contract tests stay green.

tickets.title: github-projects: reconcile/catchup — listResting + forgeCatchup over project items by Status
tickets.why: github-projects reconcile/catchup: listResting + forgeCatchup over project items.
tickets.frozen_body:
Part of #23. Core adapter (#30) and webhook lifecycle (#31) have landed.

## Problem

The `github-projects` adapter has no `catchup`/`reconcile` recovery path, so an item
missed while the receiver was down can't be replayed. Both commands hard-require
`forgeCatchup`: `agenthook reconcile` dies at `src/commands/reconcile.js:21-23`
("does not support reconcile") and `agenthook catchup <issue>` dies at
`src/commands/catchup.js:20` ("has no catchup support"). The forward-driven pipeline
has no way to recover from downtime on a Projects-v2 board.

## Evidence

- `listResting()` **already shipped** in #30 — `src/trackers/github-projects.js:444-461`,
  tested at `test/github-projects.test.js:281`. The remaining gap is only `forgeCatchup`.
- `forgeCatchup` is **absent** from the adapter's returned object
  (`src/trackers/github-projects.js:317-555`).
- Reference impl: `github.js:425-450`. Interface/return shape: `ForgedEvent` typedef
  `src/types.js:110-117`; signature `(ref, stepId?) => Promise<ForgedEvent>` at
  `src/types.js:134`.
- Server routing the forge must satisfy: `processEvents` at
  `src/trackers/github-projects.js:344-381` — `created` skips the `edited` field-value
  gate (line 359) and reads the item **live** via `itemByNodeId(node_id)` (line 367),
  routing by current Status to dedupKey `step:<id>:<ref>` (line 377).

## Proposed change

Add `forgeCatchup(ref, stepId?)` to the adapter's returned object in
`src/trackers/github-projects.js`, mirroring `github.js`:

- `findItem(ref)` to get the item's node id + current Status. **Note:** unlike the
  `github` tracker (which forges from ref+label alone), Projects-v2 routing needs the
  item `node_id`, so `findItem` always runs — passing `stepId` only skips the
  `stepByStatus` lookup, not the item fetch.
- Fail-closed: `throw` if `!issueIsOurs(it.issue)` (mirror `github.js:432`).
- Forge a **`created`** `projects_v2_item` event:
  `{ action:"created", projects_v2_item:{ node_id: it.itemId, content_type:"Issue" } }`.
  `created` avoids the `edited` path's `changes.field_value` gate; the server reads the
  item live and routes by its current Status.
- Headers: `X-GitHub-Event: projects_v2_item`, `X-GitHub-Delivery: agenthook-forge-<ref>`,
  and `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hmac>` signed with `webhookSecret()` when a secret is
  set (reuse the existing secret machinery, `github-projects.js:106-116`).
- Return `{ path:"/github-projects/", body, headers, dedupKey, stepId: step?.id }` where
  `step = stepByStatus(it.status)` and `dedupKey = step ? "step:<step.id>:<ref>" :
  "<fallback>"`. `stepId` undefined when the live Status maps to no step → `catchup`
  flags the no-op (`catchup.js:25`) instead of a false "dispatched".

## Acceptance

- [ ] `agenthook reconcile` on a `github-projects` profile replays every item resting in a
      source Status; prints `board clean` when none.
- [ ] `agenthook catchup <issue>` replays one resting item and reports the matched step;
      a not-in-a-source-Status item reports the no-op rather than "dispatched".
- [ ] Offline unit in `test/github-projects.test.js` covers `forgeCatchup` with stepId
      present (item rests in a source Status) vs undefined (Status maps to no step),
      mirroring `github.test.js:195-228`.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` green.

tickets.title: github-projects: init live-discovery + run — wizardSteps/pipelineBindings/enterStage on the Status field
tickets.why: github-projects init live-discovery + run: wizardSteps / pipeline bindings.
tickets.frozen_body:
Part of #23. **Depends on the core adapter (sub-task 1).**

## Scope

`agenthook init` live-discovery + `agenthook run` support for Projects v2 (mirror the `github`

tickets.title: dispatch: triage difficulty tag → gated model/effort escalation for the code step
tickets.why: triage difficulty tag → gated model/effort escalation — cross-cutting dispatch.
tickets.frozen_body:
## Goal

Let **triage emit a difficulty tag** (`easy|medium|hard`) that **gates the `code` step's model/effort**:
cheap model for easy/medium tickets, auto-escalate to a stronger model/effort for hard ones. This is
the difficulty-gated cascade the research points to (cheap implementation only works *where the base
model already has non-trivial success* — Snell 2024; FrugalGPT-style escalation, but placed *within*
the implementation stage of a fixed pipeline).

Pairs with the front-loaded tiering just set (triage opus/high, code sonnet/low, review opus/medium):
front-loading pays only if the cheap middle escalates on the genuinely-hard tickets.

## Mechanism (provider-blind — all in the engine, not the adapters)

1. **Verdict carries difficulty.** `src/dispatch.js` `readVerdict` already parses `outcome|target|reason`
   from the agent's verdict file — add an optional `difficulty: "easy"|"medium"|"hard"`. Triage writes
   it (instruction change, below). Validate against the enum; absent/garbage → treat as unknown (no
   escalation).
2. **Persist it per ref.** `src/store.js` — store difficulty keyed by `ref` (mirror `attempts.json`:
   `difficulty.json`). Triage's advance persists it; later steps read it. Cleared on terminal/drain
   like attempts.
3. **Gate the next step.** `src/types.js` `StepDef` gets an optional escalation block, e.g.
   `"escalate": { "hard": { "model": "claude-opus-4-8", "effort": "high" } }`. In `dispatch.js`
   `runClaude`, when resolving the spawn's `model`/`effort`, if the stored difficulty for this ref
   matches an `escalate` key, override the step's base `model`/`effort` with it. Log the escalation.
4. **Triage instruction.** `INSTRUCTIONS_TRIAGE.md` / `INSTRUCTIONS.example.md`: triage must judge
   ticket difficulty and write `difficulty` into its verdict (rubric: easy = mechanical/one-file;
   medium = normal; hard = ambiguous, cross-cutting, or novel logic).

## Acceptance

- Triage verdict with `difficulty:"hard"` → the `code` step spawns with the escalated model/effort;
  `easy`/`medium` (or absent) → the step's base model/effort. Logged either way.
- Difficulty is per-ref and cleared when the task drains/fails (no stale escalation on reuse).
- `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` green; `node --check` clean.

## Tests

`test/dispatch.test.js` (+ `store`): readVerdict parses/validates `difficulty`; the model/effort
resolver applies `escalate.hard` only when stored difficulty is `hard`; base otherwise. Pure units —
assert the resolved `(model, effort)`, no real spawn.

## Notes
- Engine-only + provider-blind (works for every tracker). No adapter changes.
- Ground in `src/dispatch.js` (`readVerdict`, `runClaude` arg build — mirrors how `model`/`effort`
  are already passed), `src/store.js` (attempts pattern), `src/types.js` (`Verdict`, `StepDef`).
- Follow-up (not this issue): the **placement-sweep experiment** that validates the whole tiering —
  freeze ~20 tickets, run strong-plan-only vs strong-code-only vs strong-review-only, compare
  accept-rate / tokens / rework. File separately when we want to run it.
